newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bill on foreign banks introduced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bill on foreign banks introduced.

text.p: A bill to give the Federal Reserve more authority to supervise foreign banks operating in the United States was introduced Friday by Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, R-New York.

D'Amato said the bill was prompted by the Daiwa Bank and Barings financial scandals. It would give the Fed authority to set conditions for the termination of a foreign bank's activities in the United States and to remove convicted felons from the banking industry.
It is unlikely any action on the bill will take place before Congress adjourns for the year next week but it can be re-introduced next year.
